title: Percentage Zone Calibrator
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Image Overlays
Grid Overlay
Percentage Rectangle Zones
Hit Testing
Responsive Coordinates
description: Drag the four corner handles of a zone over a placeholder poster and watch the pixel-to-percentage calculation for x1, y1, x2 and y2; practice matching a target within two points and predict whether a click falls inside.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Calculating percentage rectangle zones for a grid overlay
learningObjectives: The learner will calculate the x1, y1, x2 and y2 percentages of a rectangle drawn over an image and predict whether a given click falls inside it.
prerequisites: Grid Overlay and Percentage Rectangle Zones sections of Chapter 10
Converting a fraction to a percentage

accessibility.notes: describe() reports the current four percentages after every drag; handles are 24 px for touch

controls.label: Four corner handles
controls.purpose: Resize the zone; each handle sets two of x1, y1, x2, y2

controls.label: Show percentages
controls.purpose: Show or hide the calculated percentages beside the handles and in the readout

controls.label: Click test
controls.purpose: Click the picture to test whether a point is inside the zone

controls.label: Copy JSON / Hide JSON
controls.purpose: Show the zone object in data.json form

controls.label: Target practice / Check match / New target
controls.purpose: Match a random target within two percentage points per edge

controls.label: Resize picture
controls.purpose: Change the displayed picture width while the percentages stay fixed

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Direct manipulation with a live worked calculation, target matching and a click-test predictor
keyQuestions: Why does x1 stay the same when the picture is resized?
Which inequality decides whether a click is inside the zone?
How many pixels is two percentage points on this picture?
commonMisconceptions: Zone edges are stored in pixels
x2 and y2 are a width and height rather than the bottom-right corner
A click on the zone border is outside
assessmentOpportunities: Hand-calculated percentages checked against the readout
